metadata.title: Week 4 Progress
metadata.narration_policy: Narration is SCRIPT.md verbatim, one script section per beat: B00 = section 1, B01-B05 = sections 2-6, BOUT = section 7.
metadata.visual_policy: Simple illustrative Manim cards in the humanitarians palette, in the same style as the Week 1 progress video. No photos or recordings of the fellow, no person icons, no real company, product or tool logos; tools named in the narration are shown as generic drawn icons. Any file, folder, video frame or terminal shown is drawn, not a screenshot. Any checksum is a drawn fingerprint pattern, never an invented hash.
metadata.structure_note: Same simple structure as the Week 1 progress video: Claude composer cold open, five body cards, logo outro. No hesitant-writer, verdict or Your Turn beats, because the narration is the fellow's script exactly and the script has no lines for them.

fonts.latin: EB Garamond (titles and labels), Menlo (code lines)
fonts.rule: Only B01 shows Japanese. Every Manim Text containing kana or kanji sets font='Hiragino Sans' explicitly; verify the glyphs in the rendered frame, not the source.

portrait_layout.rule: In 9:16, all text and labels sit above 86% of the frame height (y < 0.86 * H), leaving the bottom 14% empty. Portrait type is large: no label smaller than the Gate T floor, and short labels over long ones.

metadata.fill_rule: Gate V needs content covering at least 55% of the safe area at 50% and at 85% of every beat (not only at the end). Each scene lays out its full cast of shapes early and holds it; elements are scaled up to fill the frame, never clustered at the top.
metadata.library_check: Searched with ./art scenes first (reel logged): quality-check lists, file checksum, folder of files, scene-by-scene review. No reusable hit for these illustrations, so B01-B05 are custom Manim. Reused: ClaudeComposerAsk / ClaudeComposerAsk916 and LogoOutro / LogoOutro916.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Keya, and I'm in week four of the Brutalist project, where I'm learning to create videos as code. The voice you're hearing is an AI voice reading my script.

show.event: the ask types in under 'Hi, Keya'
three result lines land: week 4 progress, how a video is reviewed, what I learned
the AI-voice disclosure is spoken while the answered composer holds

props.command: Help me share my week: the video I made, how a Brutalist video gets reviewed, and what I learned.

beats.narration_text: This week’s explainer is How Your Phone Types Japanese. I researched how Japanese keyboards guess which kanji you mean, wrote the script, and built the video with Claude Code.

shot.visual_intent: A title card, then a drawn keyboard guess (romaji becomes kana, the keyboard offers kanji candidates and one is marked), then three work steps: researched, wrote the script, built with Claude Code.

show.event: the title 'How Your Phone Types Japanese' draws in large, with "this week's explainer" beneath
the 'researched' step card lands at the bottom, beside two empty dashed slots
a drawn keyboard types h-a-s-h-i; an arrow turns it into the kana はし, then three kanji candidates (橋 bridge, 箸 chopsticks, 端 edge) fan out
one candidate is marked as the keyboard's guess
'wrote the script' lands in the second slot
'built with Claude Code' lands in the third slot, with a generic code-bracket icon, and the row holds

beats.narration_text: I also spent time watching Brutalist videos, and learned how a video gets reviewed: checking each claim against its sources, and watching every scene with its narration.

shot.visual_intent: A drawn video player watches a film; the review is two checks performed in turn: claims matched to sources, then scenes matched to narration.

show.event: a large drawn video frame with a play triangle and a timeline draws in, headed 'watching'
three claim cards on the left each draw an arrow to a source page on the right; each pair gets a check in turn: 'claim' to 'source'
the cards clear; a row of scene frames lines up above a matching row of narration waveforms
each scene links to its waveform and ticks: 'every scene, with its narration'

beats.narration_text: Every Brutalist video has to pass quality gates before it's final. They test layout, text size, contrast and facts. When a gate fails, you fix the scene and render it again. You never switch the check off.

shot.visual_intent: A scene token travels along four gates (layout, text size, contrast, facts). One gate fails, the token loops back through 'fix the scene' and 'render again', then passes; a gate switch stays on, with an off-switch crossed out.

show.event: four gate posts draw in along a path to 'final', labelled layout, text size, contrast, facts
the scene token passes the first gates and stops at one: a crimson cross lands on it
a loop arrow carries the token back through 'fix the scene' and 'render again'
the token passes every gate and reaches 'final'
a switch drawn 'on' with an 'off' switch crossed out: 'never switch the check off'

beats.narration_text: At the end, each final video gets a checksum, a fingerprint of the file. Anyone can use it to confirm that the video on Drive is the same one that passed the gates.

shot.visual_intent: A finished video file is stamped with a drawn fingerprint pattern; a copy on a generic drive shows the same pattern, and the two patterns are compared and match. The pattern is a drawn illustration, not a real hash.

show.event: a large video file card appears; a 'passed the gates' check lands on it
a fingerprint pattern of bars draws beside it, labelled 'checksum'
a generic cloud-drive card appears holding a copy of the video, with its own fingerprint pattern
the two patterns line up and an equals sign with a check lands: 'same file'

beats.narration_text: I learned that every part matters for a complete folder: the script, the beat sheet, the fact check, the scenes and the write-up. I've become much better at working with Claude Code in the terminal, and Humanitarians AI helped me learn that work smoothly.

shot.visual_intent: A folder fills with its five parts in spoken order; then a drawn terminal window with a skill bar growing, and a plain text badge 'Humanitarians AI' sending a 'helped' arrow to it. No logos, no person icons.

show.event: a large folder outline draws in with five empty slots
five cards land in spoken order, one per slot: script, beat sheet, fact check, scenes, write-up; the folder closes into 'complete'
a drawn terminal window opens and a progress bar grows to 'better with Claude Code'
a plain badge labelled 'Humanitarians AI' sends a 'helped' arrow to the terminal

beats.narration_text: Week 4 Progress. Built with Claude, for Humanitarians AI.

show.event: the Humanitarians AI mark springs in
the @HumanitariansAI handle settles beneath it
